scene.label: Act 3, Scene 7
scene.title: SCENE VII. London. Court of Baynard's Castle

content.text: Enter Richard and Buckingham at several doors.

lines.text: How now, how now? What say the citizens?
lines.plainText: How now how now What say the citizens

lines.text: Now, by the holy mother of our Lord,
lines.plainText: Now by the holy mother of our Lord

lines.text: The citizens are mum, say not a word.
lines.plainText: The citizens are mum say not a word

lines.text: Touched you the bastardy of Edward's children?
lines.plainText: Touched you the bastardy of Edward's children

lines.text: I did; with his contract with Lady Lucy,
lines.plainText: I did with his contract with Lady Lucy

lines.text: And his contract by deputy in France;
lines.plainText: And his contract by deputy in France

lines.text: Th' insatiate greediness of his desire,
lines.plainText: Th' insatiate greediness of his desire

lines.text: And his enforcement of the city wives;
lines.plainText: And his enforcement of the city wives

lines.text: His tyranny for trifles; his own bastardy,
lines.plainText: His tyranny for trifles his own bastardy

lines.text: As being got, your father then in France,
lines.plainText: As being got your father then in France

lines.text: And his resemblance, being not like the Duke.
lines.plainText: And his resemblance being not like the Duke

lines.text: Withal, I did infer your lineaments,
lines.plainText: Withal I did infer your lineaments

lines.text: Being the right idea of your father,
lines.plainText: Being the right idea of your father

lines.text: Both in your form and nobleness of mind;
lines.plainText: Both in your form and nobleness of mind

lines.text: Laid open all your victories in Scotland,
lines.plainText: Laid open all your victories in Scotland

lines.text: Your discipline in war, wisdom in peace,
lines.plainText: Your discipline in war wisdom in peace

lines.text: Your bounty, virtue, fair humility;
lines.plainText: Your bounty virtue fair humility

lines.text: Indeed, left nothing fitting for your purpose
lines.plainText: Indeed left nothing fitting for your purpose

lines.text: Untouched or slightly handled in discourse.
lines.plainText: Untouched or slightly handled in discourse

lines.text: And when mine oratory drew toward end,
lines.plainText: And when mine oratory drew toward end

lines.text: I bid them that did love their country's good
lines.plainText: I bid them that did love their country's good

lines.text: Cry "God save Richard, England's royal King!"
lines.plainText: Cry God save Richard England's royal King

lines.text: And did they so?
lines.plainText: And did they so

lines.text: No, so God help me, they spake not a word,
lines.plainText: No so God help me they spake not a word

lines.text: But, like dumb statues or breathing stones,
lines.plainText: But like dumb statues or breathing stones

lines.text: Stared each on other, and looked deadly pale.
lines.plainText: Stared each on other and looked deadly pale

lines.text: Which when I saw, I reprehended them,
lines.plainText: Which when I saw I reprehended them

lines.text: And asked the Mayor what meant this wilful silence.
lines.plainText: And asked the Mayor what meant this wilful silence

lines.text: His answer was, the people were not used
lines.plainText: His answer was the people were not used

lines.text: To be spoke to but by the Recorder.
lines.plainText: To be spoke to but by the Recorder

lines.text: Then he was urged to tell my tale again:
lines.plainText: Then he was urged to tell my tale again

lines.text: "Thus saith the Duke, thus hath the Duke inferred"
lines.plainText: Thus saith the Duke thus hath the Duke inferred

lines.text: But nothing spoke in warrant from himself.
lines.plainText: But nothing spoke in warrant from himself

lines.text: When he had done, some followers of mine own,
lines.plainText: When he had done some followers of mine own

lines.text: At lower end of the hall, hurled up their caps,
lines.plainText: At lower end of the hall hurled up their caps

lines.text: And some ten voices cried, "God save King Richard!"
lines.plainText: And some ten voices cried God save King Richard

lines.text: And thus I took the vantage of those few.
lines.plainText: And thus I took the vantage of those few

lines.text: "Thanks, gentle citizens and friends," quoth I;
lines.plainText: Thanks gentle citizens and friends quoth I

lines.text: "This general applause and cheerful shout
lines.plainText: This general applause and cheerful shout

lines.text: Argues your wisdoms and your love to Richard."
lines.plainText: Argues your wisdoms and your love to Richard

lines.text: And even here brake off and came away.
lines.plainText: And even here brake off and came away

lines.text: What, tongueless blocks were they! Would they not speak?
lines.plainText: What tongueless blocks were they Would they not speak

lines.text: Will not the Mayor then and his brethren, come?
lines.plainText: Will not the Mayor then and his brethren come

lines.text: The mayor is here at hand. Intend some fear;
lines.plainText: The mayor is here at hand Intend some fear

lines.text: Be not you spoke with but by mighty suit.
lines.plainText: Be not you spoke with but by mighty suit

lines.text: And look you get a prayer-book in your hand,
lines.plainText: And look you get a prayerbook in your hand

lines.text: And stand between two churchmen, good my lord,
lines.plainText: And stand between two churchmen good my lord

lines.text: For on that ground I'll make a holy descant.
lines.plainText: For on that ground I'll make a holy descant

lines.text: And be not easily won to our requests.
lines.plainText: And be not easily won to our requests

lines.text: Play the maid's part: still answer nay, and take it.
lines.plainText: Play the maid's part still answer nay and take it

lines.text: I go, and if you plead as well for them
lines.plainText: I go and if you plead as well for them

lines.text: As I can say nay to thee for myself,
lines.plainText: As I can say nay to thee for myself

lines.text: No doubt we bring it to a happy issue.
lines.plainText: No doubt we bring it to a happy issue

lines.text: Go, go, up to the leads, the Lord Mayor knocks.
lines.plainText: Go go up to the leads the Lord Mayor knocks

content.text: Enter the Lord Mayor and Citizens.

lines.text: He doth entreat your Grace, my noble lord,
lines.plainText: He doth entreat your Grace my noble lord

lines.text: To visit him tomorrow or next day.
lines.plainText: To visit him tomorrow or next day

lines.text: He is within, with two right reverend fathers,
lines.plainText: He is within with two right reverend fathers

lines.text: Divinely bent to meditation;
lines.plainText: Divinely bent to meditation

lines.text: And in no worldly suits would he be moved
lines.plainText: And in no worldly suits would he be moved

lines.text: To draw him from his holy exercise.
lines.plainText: To draw him from his holy exercise

lines.text: Return, good Catesby, to the gracious Duke;
lines.plainText: Return good Catesby to the gracious Duke

lines.text: Tell him myself, the Mayor and aldermen,
lines.plainText: Tell him myself the Mayor and aldermen

lines.text: In deep designs, in matter of great moment,
lines.plainText: In deep designs in matter of great moment

lines.text: No less importing than our general good,
lines.plainText: No less importing than our general good

lines.text: Are come to have some conference with his Grace.
lines.plainText: Are come to have some conference with his Grace

lines.text: I'll signify so much unto him straight.
lines.plainText: I'll signify so much unto him straight

lines.text: Ah ha, my lord, this prince is not an Edward!
lines.plainText: Ah ha my lord this prince is not an Edward

lines.text: He is not lolling on a lewd love-bed,
lines.plainText: He is not lolling on a lewd lovebed

lines.text: But on his knees at meditation;
lines.plainText: But on his knees at meditation

lines.text: Not dallying with a brace of courtesans,
lines.plainText: Not dallying with a brace of courtesans

lines.text: But meditating with two deep divines;
lines.plainText: But meditating with two deep divines

lines.text: Not sleeping, to engross his idle body,
lines.plainText: Not sleeping to engross his idle body

lines.text: But praying, to enrich his watchful soul.
lines.plainText: But praying to enrich his watchful soul

lines.text: Happy were England would this virtuous prince
lines.plainText: Happy were England would this virtuous prince

lines.text: Take on his Grace the sovereignty thereof.
lines.plainText: Take on his Grace the sovereignty thereof

lines.text: But sure I fear we shall not win him to it.
lines.plainText: But sure I fear we shall not win him to it

lines.text: Marry, God defend his Grace should say us nay!
lines.plainText: Marry God defend his Grace should say us nay

lines.text: I fear he will. Here Catesby comes again.
lines.plainText: I fear he will Here Catesby comes again

lines.text: He wonders to what end you have assembled
lines.plainText: He wonders to what end you have assembled

lines.text: Such troops of citizens to come to him,
lines.plainText: Such troops of citizens to come to him

lines.text: His Grace not being warned thereof before.
lines.plainText: His Grace not being warned thereof before

lines.text: He fears, my lord, you mean no good to him.
lines.plainText: He fears my lord you mean no good to him

lines.text: Sorry I am my noble cousin should
lines.plainText: Sorry I am my noble cousin should

lines.text: Suspect me that I mean no good to him.
lines.plainText: Suspect me that I mean no good to him

lines.text: By heaven, we come to him in perfect love,
lines.plainText: By heaven we come to him in perfect love

lines.text: And so once more return and tell his Grace.
lines.plainText: And so once more return and tell his Grace

content.text: Enter Richard aloft, between two Bishops. Catesby reenters.

lines.text: See where his Grace stands 'tween two clergymen!
lines.plainText: See where his Grace stands 'tween two clergymen

lines.text: Two props of virtue for a Christian prince,
lines.plainText: Two props of virtue for a Christian prince

lines.text: To stay him from the fall of vanity;
lines.plainText: To stay him from the fall of vanity

lines.text: And, see, a book of prayer in his hand,
lines.plainText: And see a book of prayer in his hand

lines.text: True ornaments to know a holy man.
lines.plainText: True ornaments to know a holy man

lines.text: Famous Plantagenet, most gracious Prince,
lines.plainText: Famous Plantagenet most gracious Prince

lines.text: Lend favourable ear to our requests,
lines.plainText: Lend favourable ear to our requests

lines.text: And pardon us the interruption
lines.plainText: And pardon us the interruption

lines.text: Of thy devotion and right Christian zeal.
lines.plainText: Of thy devotion and right Christian zeal

lines.text: My lord, there needs no such apology.
lines.plainText: My lord there needs no such apology

lines.text: I do beseech your Grace to pardon me,
lines.plainText: I do beseech your Grace to pardon me

lines.text: Who, earnest in the service of my God,
lines.plainText: Who earnest in the service of my God

lines.text: Deferred the visitation of my friends.
lines.plainText: Deferred the visitation of my friends

lines.text: But, leaving this, what is your Grace's pleasure?
lines.plainText: But leaving this what is your Grace's pleasure

lines.text: Even that, I hope, which pleaseth God above,
lines.plainText: Even that I hope which pleaseth God above

lines.text: And all good men of this ungoverned isle.
lines.plainText: And all good men of this ungoverned isle

lines.text: I do suspect I have done some offence
lines.plainText: I do suspect I have done some offence

lines.text: That seems disgracious in the city's eye,
lines.plainText: That seems disgracious in the city's eye

lines.text: And that you come to reprehend my ignorance.
lines.plainText: And that you come to reprehend my ignorance

lines.text: You have, my lord. Would it might please your Grace,
lines.plainText: You have my lord Would it might please your Grace

lines.text: On our entreaties, to amend your fault.
lines.plainText: On our entreaties to amend your fault

lines.text: Else wherefore breathe I in a Christian land?
lines.plainText: Else wherefore breathe I in a Christian land

lines.text: Know then, it is your fault that you resign
lines.plainText: Know then it is your fault that you resign

lines.text: The supreme seat, the throne majestical,
lines.plainText: The supreme seat the throne majestical

lines.text: The sceptered office of your ancestors,
lines.plainText: The sceptered office of your ancestors

lines.text: Your state of fortune, and your due of birth,
lines.plainText: Your state of fortune and your due of birth

lines.text: The lineal glory of your royal house,
lines.plainText: The lineal glory of your royal house

lines.text: To the corruption of a blemished stock;
lines.plainText: To the corruption of a blemished stock

lines.text: Whiles in the mildness of your sleepy thoughts,
lines.plainText: Whiles in the mildness of your sleepy thoughts

lines.text: Which here we waken to our country's good,
lines.plainText: Which here we waken to our country's good

lines.text: The noble isle doth want her proper limbs;
lines.plainText: The noble isle doth want her proper limbs

lines.text: Her face defaced with scars of infamy,
lines.plainText: Her face defaced with scars of infamy

lines.text: Her royal stock graft with ignoble plants,
lines.plainText: Her royal stock graft with ignoble plants

lines.text: And almost shouldered in the swallowing gulf
lines.plainText: And almost shouldered in the swallowing gulf

lines.text: Of dark forgetfulness and deep oblivion;
lines.plainText: Of dark forgetfulness and deep oblivion

lines.text: Which to recure, we heartily solicit
lines.plainText: Which to recure we heartily solicit

lines.text: Your gracious self to take on you the charge
lines.plainText: Your gracious self to take on you the charge

lines.text: And kingly government of this your land,
lines.plainText: And kingly government of this your land

lines.text: Not as Protector, steward, substitute,
lines.plainText: Not as Protector steward substitute

lines.text: Or lowly factor for another's gain,
lines.plainText: Or lowly factor for another's gain

lines.text: But as successively, from blood to blood,
lines.plainText: But as successively from blood to blood

lines.text: Your right of birth, your empery, your own.
lines.plainText: Your right of birth your empery your own

lines.text: For this, consorted with the citizens,
lines.plainText: For this consorted with the citizens

lines.text: Your very worshipful and loving friends,
lines.plainText: Your very worshipful and loving friends

lines.text: And by their vehement instigation,
lines.plainText: And by their vehement instigation

lines.text: In this just cause come I to move your Grace.
lines.plainText: In this just cause come I to move your Grace

lines.text: I cannot tell if to depart in silence
lines.plainText: I cannot tell if to depart in silence

lines.text: Or bitterly to speak in your reproof
lines.plainText: Or bitterly to speak in your reproof

lines.text: Best fitteth my degree or your condition.
lines.plainText: Best fitteth my degree or your condition

lines.text: If not to answer, you might haply think
lines.plainText: If not to answer you might haply think

lines.text: Tongue-tied ambition, not replying, yielded
lines.plainText: Tonguetied ambition not replying yielded

lines.text: To bear the golden yoke of sovereignty,
lines.plainText: To bear the golden yoke of sovereignty

lines.text: Which fondly you would here impose on me;
lines.plainText: Which fondly you would here impose on me

lines.text: If to reprove you for this suit of yours,
lines.plainText: If to reprove you for this suit of yours

lines.text: So seasoned with your faithful love to me,
lines.plainText: So seasoned with your faithful love to me

lines.text: Then, on the other side, I checked my friends.
lines.plainText: Then on the other side I checked my friends

lines.text: Therefore, to speak, and to avoid the first,
lines.plainText: Therefore to speak and to avoid the first

lines.text: And then, in speaking, not to incur the last,
lines.plainText: And then in speaking not to incur the last

lines.text: Definitively thus I answer you:
lines.plainText: Definitively thus I answer you

lines.text: Your love deserves my thanks, but my desert
lines.plainText: Your love deserves my thanks but my desert

lines.text: Unmeritable shuns your high request.
lines.plainText: Unmeritable shuns your high request

lines.text: First, if all obstacles were cut away,
lines.plainText: First if all obstacles were cut away

lines.text: And that my path were even to the crown
lines.plainText: And that my path were even to the crown

lines.text: As the ripe revenue and due of birth,
lines.plainText: As the ripe revenue and due of birth

lines.text: Yet so much is my poverty of spirit,
lines.plainText: Yet so much is my poverty of spirit

lines.text: So mighty and so many my defects,
lines.plainText: So mighty and so many my defects

lines.text: That I would rather hide me from my greatness,
lines.plainText: That I would rather hide me from my greatness

lines.text: Being a bark to brook no mighty sea,
lines.plainText: Being a bark to brook no mighty sea

lines.text: Than in my greatness covet to be hid,
lines.plainText: Than in my greatness covet to be hid

lines.text: And in the vapour of my glory smothered.
lines.plainText: And in the vapour of my glory smothered

lines.text: But, God be thanked, there is no need of me,
lines.plainText: But God be thanked there is no need of me

lines.text: And much I need to help you, were there need.
lines.plainText: And much I need to help you were there need

lines.text: The royal tree hath left us royal fruit,
lines.plainText: The royal tree hath left us royal fruit

lines.text: Which, mellowed by the stealing hours of time,
lines.plainText: Which mellowed by the stealing hours of time

lines.text: Will well become the seat of majesty,
lines.plainText: Will well become the seat of majesty

lines.text: And make, no doubt, us happy by his reign.
lines.plainText: And make no doubt us happy by his reign

lines.text: On him I lay that you would lay on me,
lines.plainText: On him I lay that you would lay on me

lines.text: The right and fortune of his happy stars,
lines.plainText: The right and fortune of his happy stars

lines.text: Which God defend that I should wring from him.
lines.plainText: Which God defend that I should wring from him

lines.text: My lord, this argues conscience in your Grace;
lines.plainText: My lord this argues conscience in your Grace

lines.text: But the respects thereof are nice and trivial,
lines.plainText: But the respects thereof are nice and trivial

lines.text: All circumstances well considered.
lines.plainText: All circumstances well considered

lines.text: You say that Edward is your brother's son;
lines.plainText: You say that Edward is your brother's son

lines.text: So say we too, but not by Edward's wife.
lines.plainText: So say we too but not by Edward's wife

lines.text: For first was he contract to Lady Lucy
lines.plainText: For first was he contract to Lady Lucy

lines.text: Your mother lives a witness to his vow,
lines.plainText: Your mother lives a witness to his vow

lines.text: And afterward by substitute betrothed
lines.plainText: And afterward by substitute betrothed

lines.text: To Bona, sister to the King of France.
lines.plainText: To Bona sister to the King of France

lines.text: These both put off, a poor petitioner,
lines.plainText: These both put off a poor petitioner

lines.text: A care-crazed mother to a many sons,
lines.plainText: A carecrazed mother to a many sons

lines.text: A beauty-waning and distressed widow,
lines.plainText: A beautywaning and distressed widow

lines.text: Even in the afternoon of her best days,
lines.plainText: Even in the afternoon of her best days

lines.text: Made prize and purchase of his wanton eye,
lines.plainText: Made prize and purchase of his wanton eye

lines.text: Seduced the pitch and height of his degree
lines.plainText: Seduced the pitch and height of his degree

lines.text: To base declension and loathed bigamy.
lines.plainText: To base declension and loathed bigamy

lines.text: By her, in his unlawful bed, he got
lines.plainText: By her in his unlawful bed he got

lines.text: This Edward, whom our manners call the Prince.
lines.plainText: This Edward whom our manners call the Prince

lines.text: More bitterly could I expostulate,
lines.plainText: More bitterly could I expostulate

lines.text: Save that, for reverence to some alive,
lines.plainText: Save that for reverence to some alive

lines.text: I give a sparing limit to my tongue.
lines.plainText: I give a sparing limit to my tongue

lines.text: Then, good my lord, take to your royal self
lines.plainText: Then good my lord take to your royal self

lines.text: This proffered benefit of dignity,
lines.plainText: This proffered benefit of dignity

lines.text: If not to bless us and the land withal,
lines.plainText: If not to bless us and the land withal

lines.text: Yet to draw forth your noble ancestry
lines.plainText: Yet to draw forth your noble ancestry

lines.text: From the corruption of abusing times
lines.plainText: From the corruption of abusing times

lines.text: Unto a lineal true-derived course.
lines.plainText: Unto a lineal truederived course

lines.text: Do, good my lord. Your citizens entreat you.
lines.plainText: Do good my lord Your citizens entreat you

lines.text: Refuse not, mighty lord, this proffered love.
lines.plainText: Refuse not mighty lord this proffered love

lines.text: O, make them joyful; grant their lawful suit.
lines.plainText: O make them joyful grant their lawful suit

lines.text: Alas, why would you heap those cares on me?
lines.plainText: Alas why would you heap those cares on me

lines.text: I am unfit for state and majesty.
lines.plainText: I am unfit for state and majesty

lines.text: I do beseech you, take it not amiss;
lines.plainText: I do beseech you take it not amiss

lines.text: I cannot, nor I will not, yield to you.
lines.plainText: I cannot nor I will not yield to you

lines.text: If you refuse it, as in love and zeal
lines.plainText: If you refuse it as in love and zeal

lines.text: Loath to depose the child, your brother's son—
lines.plainText: Loath to depose the child your brother's son

lines.text: As well we know your tenderness of heart
lines.plainText: As well we know your tenderness of heart

lines.text: And gentle, kind, effeminate remorse,
lines.plainText: And gentle kind effeminate remorse

lines.text: Which we have noted in you to your kindred,
lines.plainText: Which we have noted in you to your kindred

lines.text: And equally indeed to all estates—
lines.plainText: And equally indeed to all estates

lines.text: Yet know, whe'er you accept our suit or no,
lines.plainText: Yet know whe'er you accept our suit or no

lines.text: Your brother's son shall never reign our king,
lines.plainText: Your brother's son shall never reign our king

lines.text: But we will plant some other in the throne,
lines.plainText: But we will plant some other in the throne

lines.text: To the disgrace and downfall of your house.
lines.plainText: To the disgrace and downfall of your house

lines.plainText: And in this resolution here we leave you

lines.plainText: Come citizens zounds I'll entreat no more

lines.plainText: Call him again sweet Prince accept their suit

lines.text: If you deny them, all the land will rue it.
lines.plainText: If you deny them all the land will rue it

lines.plainText: Will you enforce me to a world of cares

lines.plainText: Call them again I am not made of stones

lines.text: But penetrable to your kind entreaties,
lines.plainText: But penetrable to your kind entreaties

lines.text: Albeit against my conscience and my soul.
lines.plainText: Albeit against my conscience and my soul

lines.plainText: In saying so you shall but say the truth

lines.plainText: Then I salute you with this royal title

lines.plainText: Long live King Richard England's worthy King

lines.text: Amen.
lines.plainText: Amen

lines.text: Tomorrow may it please you to be crowned?
lines.plainText: Tomorrow may it please you to be crowned

lines.text: Even when you please, for you will have it so.
lines.plainText: Even when you please for you will have it so

lines.plainText: Tomorrow then we will attend your Grace
